label: First token is one of h,e,j,c,u,3,g,x,i,f; plus <DEL> in length-3 sequences and h at step 2
explanation: An update-gate unit that fires only early in the sequence (original steps t<=4 and the <DEL> step) and almost never during the copy phase. Its main mode, about 52% of activation mass, is step 0 when the first token is one of h,e,j,c,u,3,g,x,i,f. Precision is 1.0 there and the unit never fires at t=0 on any other token; h at t=0 gives the largest values. The strongest activations are at <DEL> when L=3 (precision 0.98, about 11% of mass; the top examples are all short sequences), and the unit is also active on h at t=2 (precision 0.93). The same token set also produces weak, context-dependent activations at t=1..4, nearly always on a token occurrence that is the first in the sequence, but those are not predictable from token and position alone (precision about 0.2-0.3). This tail is the unexplained ~28% of mass. Never active at t>=5 or past the first copy output, and rarely on d or on repeated tokens. Dev: P 0.99, R 0.63, F1 0.77, mass recall 0.72.
